questions.text: Which equation of motion relates v, u, a and s (constant acceleration)?
questions.explanation: For constant acceleration, v^2 = u^2 + 2as directly links final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and displacement.

questions.text: The unit of work done (SI) is:
questions.explanation: Work is measured in Joule (J) in SI.

questions.text: Newton's second law is best stated as:
questions.explanation: For constant mass, force equals rate of change of momentum, which simplifies to F = ma.

questions.text: A common way to reduce silly mistakes in numericals is to:
options: Track mistake patterns and use a checklist
questions.explanation: A small checklist (units, sign, substitution) and mistake logs significantly reduce repeated errors.

questions.text: Work done by a constant force F making angle θ with displacement s is:
questions.explanation: Work is the dot product: W = F · s = Fs cosθ.

questions.text: The area under a velocity–time graph represents:
questions.explanation: Area under v–t curve gives displacement (or distance if velocity is always positive).

questions.text: Coulomb's law states that the force between two point charges is proportional to:
options: Product of charges and inverse square of distance
Sum of charges and inverse distance
Product of charges and square of distance
Difference of charges and inverse square of distance
questions.explanation: F ∝ q1q2/r^2 (along the line joining charges).

questions.text: Electric field at a point is defined as:
questions.explanation: E = F/q is the force experienced by a small positive test charge per unit charge.

questions.text: The SI unit of electric potential is:
questions.explanation: Electric potential is measured in Volt (V).

questions.text: Capacitance is defined as:
questions.explanation: Capacitance C = Q/V.

questions.text: If the distance between two charges is doubled, the Coulomb force becomes:
questions.explanation: Since F ∝ 1/r^2, doubling r makes force 1/4.

questions.text: Electric field lines never:
questions.explanation: Intersection would imply two directions of field at one point, which is not possible.

questions.text: Lens formula (Cartesian sign convention) is:
questions.explanation: For thin lenses: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u (with sign convention).

questions.text: Power of a lens is measured in:
questions.explanation: Lens power P = 1/f (in meters) and unit is Dioptre (D).

questions.text: For a concave mirror, a real image is formed when the object is placed:
questions.explanation: For concave mirror, object beyond focus forms a real inverted image.

questions.text: Magnification for a lens is given by:
questions.explanation: For a thin lens, linear magnification m = v/u (with sign convention).

questions.text: In Young's double slit experiment, fringe width is directly proportional to:
questions.explanation: β = λD/d, so it increases with D.

questions.text: A prism disperses white light because refractive index depends on:
questions.explanation: Refractive index varies with wavelength, causing different colors to deviate differently.

questions.text: 1 mole of any substance contains:
questions.explanation: Avogadro's number is approximately 6.022×10^23.

questions.text: Ideal gas equation is:
questions.explanation: Ideal gas law: PV = nRT.

questions.text: Gibbs free energy relation is:
questions.explanation: G = H - TS.

questions.text: At equilibrium, the reaction quotient Q equals:
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, Q = K.

questions.text: Enthalpy is denoted by:
questions.explanation: Enthalpy is represented by H.

questions.text: For an exothermic reaction, ΔH is:
questions.explanation: Heat is released, so ΔH is negative.

questions.text: Inductive effect is transmitted through:
questions.explanation: Inductive effect is polarization through sigma bonds.

questions.text: Resonance involves movement of:
questions.explanation: Resonance is delocalization of pi electrons and lone pairs.

questions.text: The hybridization of carbon in methane (CH4) is:
questions.explanation: Methane has tetrahedral geometry with sp3 hybridization.

questions.text: Number of structural isomers of C4H10 is:
questions.explanation: Butane has two structural isomers: n-butane and isobutane.

questions.text: A carbocation is:
questions.explanation: Carbocation has a positive charge on carbon.

questions.text: Which is generally the most stabilizing effect (approx.)?
questions.explanation: Resonance typically offers strong stabilization, often greater than hyperconjugation.

questions.text: Across a period, atomic size generally:
questions.explanation: Effective nuclear charge increases across a period, pulling electrons closer.

questions.text: Down a group, electronegativity generally:
questions.explanation: Atomic size increases down the group, reducing attraction for bonding electrons.

questions.text: Hybridization of carbon in ethene (C2H4) is:
questions.explanation: Ethene has a double bond and trigonal planar geometry (sp2).

questions.text: Ionic bonds form due to:
questions.explanation: Ionic bond arises due to electron transfer and electrostatic attraction.

questions.text: Which is more electronegative?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity.

questions.text: The shape of BF3 is:
questions.explanation: BF3 has sp2 hybridization and trigonal planar geometry.

questions.text: The functional unit of kidney is:
questions.explanation: Nephron is the functional unit of kidney.

questions.text: Oxygen is mainly transported in blood by:
questions.explanation: Most oxygen is carried bound to hemoglobin in RBCs.

questions.text: Heart chambers are separated by:
questions.explanation: Septa separate the chambers of the heart.

questions.text: The primary site of nutrient absorption in humans is:
questions.explanation: Most nutrient absorption happens in the small intestine (villi).

questions.text: During inspiration, diaphragm moves:
questions.explanation: Diaphragm contracts and moves downward, increasing thoracic volume.

questions.text: The normal pH of human blood is around:
questions.explanation: Blood pH is tightly regulated around 7.35–7.45.

questions.text: Mendel's law of segregation states that:
questions.explanation: Each gamete receives only one allele of a gene due to segregation.

questions.text: DNA is a polymer of:
questions.explanation: DNA is made of nucleotide monomers.

questions.text: The process of copying DNA is called:
questions.explanation: Replication produces an identical DNA copy.

questions.text: A heterozygous genotype for a trait is represented as:
questions.explanation: Heterozygous means two different alleles: Aa.

questions.text: In a monohybrid cross (Aa × Aa), the phenotypic ratio is:
questions.explanation: Dominant:recessive phenotypic ratio is 3:1.

questions.text: RNA differs from DNA primarily by:
questions.explanation: RNA uses uracil (U) instead of thymine (T) and has ribose sugar.

questions.text: The term 'ecosystem' includes:
questions.explanation: An ecosystem includes biotic and abiotic components interacting together.

questions.text: Primary producers in an ecosystem are usually:
questions.explanation: Green plants (autotrophs) produce food via photosynthesis.

questions.text: Energy transfer between trophic levels is roughly:
questions.explanation: Only about 10% energy is transferred to the next trophic level (Lindeman's law).

questions.text: Biodiversity hotspots are regions with:
questions.explanation: Hotspots have many endemic species and significant habitat loss.

questions.text: Ozone layer depletion is mainly caused by:
questions.explanation: CFCs release chlorine radicals that destroy ozone.

questions.text: Decomposers are important because they:
options: Recycle nutrients back to the ecosystem
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down organic matter and return nutrients to the soil/water.
